title: Memory will grow forever in a TileMapLayer when cells generate and delete further away
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in 4.7.2-stable, 4.6-stable, 4.5-stable
- Not Reproducible in 4.3-stable, 4.4-stable, 4.41-stable

### System information

Godot v4.7.2.stable - Windows 11 (build 26300) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Direct3D 12 (Mobile) - dedicated Intel(R) Graphics (Intel Corporation; 31.0.101.4953) - Intel(R) Core(TM) 7 150U (12 threads) - 15.69 GiB memory - WASAPI (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

When I was working with chunk generation, I noticed a subtle bug in the engine. I made sure to precisely manage how memory works in my chunk generation game but there appears to be some sort of memory leak... not directly a leak per say just memory grows forever when it shouldn't. This appears to occur when creating many cells farther away from the original spot. While albeit reasonable, those same cells get erased. So what appears to happen is your able to "load" and "unload" chunks but objects will grow and so will memory grow. From my findings it appears the "DebugQuadrant" is causing this issue. 

### Steps to reproduce

1. Add a TileMapLayer to scene
2. Write a script that loads and unlocks cells (I did mine as 16 x 16 as in 256 cells)
3. Make sure to add chunks to array and remove it when not needed
4. Have the chunks generate and unload forever while going further in position in an incremental way

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[tile-map-layer-debug-quadrant-bug.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33584112/tile-map-layer-debug-quadrant-bug.zip)
